SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
SATURDAY - JANUARY 28, 2023 - 10:00 A.M.
SIERRA ROOM - CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING ARTS
18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the Sierra Room will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting in-person in the Sierra Room at the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on Friday, January 27, 2023. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD SATURDAY,
JANUARY 28, 2023, 10:00 A.M., IN THE SIERRA ROOM AT CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE
PERFORMING ARTS, 18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 10:00 a.m.

2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor/Chair Vo.

3.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Bruce Barrows
  Mayor/Chair Chuong Vo

  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki was noted absent for the record.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to excuse Council/Agency
  Member Solanki from the Saturday, January 28, 2023, 10:00 a.m. Special Meeting
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki
  ABSTAIN:  None

  The following is noted for the meeting record: At 11:53 a.m. Council/Agency Member
  Yokoyama left his seat at the dais, exited the room, and was noted absent from the
  meeting. At 1:00 p.m. Council/Agency Member Solanki arrived to the room, assumed his
  seat at the dais, and was noted present for the remainder of the meeting. At 1:15 p.m.
  Council/Agency Member Yokoyama returned to the room, assumed his seat at the dais,
  and was noted as present for the remainder of the meeting.

4.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Public comments were opened throughout the special meeting and are consolidated in this
  section.

  Norma Williamson suggested prioritizing the addition of recycling bins in public places and
  the addition of pickleball courts throughout the community.

  Teddy Lloyd suggested prioritizing the addition of pickleball courts throughout the
  community.

  Murali Vasudevan suggested prioritizing resolving financial matters at the Cerritos Center for
  the Performing Arts and Cerritos Electric Utility and maintaining sidewalks, roads, and parks.

  Marty Grossman suggested prioritizing resolving financial losses at the Cerritos Center for
  the Performing Arts, including allowing the community to select performances which will
  increase revenue.

4.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Gail Grossman suggested prioritizing additional services for seniors, increasing cable
  service provider choices, reducing financial contributions to the Chamber of Commerce,
  and increasing street maintenance and repair in the community.

  Case van der Linden suggested prioritizing the inclusion of deep root watering
  techniques for newly planted City trees. The speaker also requested the ABC Unified
  School District offer their excess solar power to residents for purchase. In conclusion,
  the speaker agreed with the five (5) Strategic Plan goals which were developed through
  City Council consensus and thanked the City Council for conducting the Strategic Plan
  study session. (The Strategic Plan goals are listed under agenda item 5 in the following
  section of this document).

  John Cabula suggested prioritizing homelessness and related services to the homeless
  community in Cerritos.

  Daisy Lagasca requested the City Council prioritize the community’s input when
  developing the City’s Strategic Plan goals.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Steve Hsieh suggested prioritizing road repair and maintenance, addressing pine trees
  and other trees causing damage, and street and traffic light maintenance.

  Murali Vasudevan suggested additional Strategic Plan study sessions for additional
  community input and offered his suggestions for prioritizing Strategic Plan goals.

5.  New Business

5A.  Review and consideration of existing environmental factors and current economic
  conditions for the Cerritos City Council to establish the priority goals to guide the
  preparation of the City's Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Budget and Strategic Financial Plan in
  accordance with the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget Preparation Policy (Policy No.
  2.04) (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  A staff report was given by the City’s Strategic Plan Committee: Torrey Contreras,
  Senior Assistant City Manager/Committee Chair, Ryan Carey, Finance Manager, Peter
  Kemp, Budget Manager, and Jeff Thielke, Theater Executive Director. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments (Public comments are memorialized under item 4 of
  this document). Discussion ensued among the City Council, members of the public, and
  City staff regarding the various proposed Strategic Plan goals.

  Upon completion of a goal prioritization exercise facilitated by the City’s Strategic Plan
  Committee, the following five Fiscal Year 2023-24 Strategic Plan goals were established
  via unanimous (5 – 0) City Council consensus and are listed below in priority order (with
  1 representing the highest priority):

  1.  Increase Tree and Street Maintenance/Repair
  2.  Increase Sales Tax Revenue
  3.  Review Contract Law Enforcement Services
  4.  Increase Technology Infrastructure/Use
  5.  Increase Fiscal Transparency

  The meeting adjourned at 2:30 p.m.
